AttributionOut.description:
A data licence's required credit, to show wherever the finding is shown
(e.g. "Weather data by Open-Meteo.com", linking `url`).
AttributionOut.title: AttributionOut

AuthMethodsOut.description: How someone may sign in on the host this was asked on (YONDER-180).
AuthMethodsOut.title: AuthMethodsOut

BudgetBatchIn.description:
An agent's budget research (the trip-budget research kit, D-180). Every
item lands as a draft; `replace` first drops your earlier drafts in the same
categories. Kept items are never touched.
BudgetBatchIn.title: BudgetBatchIn

BudgetItemIn.description:
Plan a cost for the travellers it's for (`traveler_ids`; your own entry
defaults to you, research must name them). `amount` is the one estimated
amount for them — a room for two is one cost; nothing is multiplied (D-179).
`start_date`–`end_date` say when it applies, if not the whole trip.
BudgetItemIn.title: BudgetItemIn

BudgetItemOut.description:
A planned cost (D-178/D-179/D-184): one estimated amount for the travellers
tagged on it — never multiplied by people or days. `total` is it in the trip
currency.
BudgetItemOut.title: BudgetItemOut

BudgetItemPatch.description:
Edit a planned item; editing an agent's draft keeps it. `status: "kept"`
keeps a draft as it is.
BudgetItemPatch.title: BudgetItemPatch

DiscoverIn.description:
Optional: refresh one topic (weather, currency, food…), or one topic for
one place (`place_key` as on the finding, e.g. "PT:Lisbon"), instead of
the whole suite.
DiscoverIn.title: DiscoverIn

DiscoveryItemOut.description:
A place, event or activity inside a Food & Drink or Events & Activities
finding (4.5, YONDER-147). `finding_id` ties it to its city's write-up.
DiscoveryItemOut.title: DiscoveryItemOut

DiscoveryPlaceOut.description:
One place Discovery will research on a trip, for the caller (YONDER-264).
`is_home`: home, never researched. `home_country`: in the home country, so the
local topics are skipped. `excluded`: the caller chose to skip it.
DiscoveryPlaceOut.title: DiscoveryPlaceOut

DiscoveryStatusOut.description:
The caller's OWN Discovery run on a trip (YONDER-238; runs are per person,
4.1) — what the app's Run / Refresh button and progress bar poll.
DiscoveryStatusOut.title: DiscoveryStatusOut

ExpenseCommentOut.description: A comment on an actual expense (D-185).
ExpenseCommentOut.title: ExpenseCommentOut

ExpenseIn.description:
Record an expense. `traveler_ids` is who it's split equally between
([]/omitted = everyone on the trip); for `split: "exact"` send `shares`
({traveler_id: amount}) adding up to `amount`. Leave `rate` blank to use the
trip's rate for that day (D-195); give it to override.
ExpenseIn.title: ExpenseIn

ExpensePatch.description:
Edit an expense. Only the fields sent change; changing amount, currency or
split recomputes the shares. `activity_id: ""` unlinks the timeline item.
ExpensePatch.title: ExpensePatch

FindingIn.description:
A finding from an external agent for the caller's Discover tab (YONDER-108).
Food/events may carry `items` (4.5); language_local carries `phrases`.
FindingIn.title: FindingIn

ItemIn.description:
A place, event or activity an agent adds to a Food & Drink or Events &
Activities finding (4.5, YONDER-148). Only `kind` and `name` are required.
ItemIn.title: ItemIn

ItemToTimelineIn.description:
Add a Discover item to the timeline (4.5). The activity is built from the
item (name, address, map link, website, what to get); give the time.
ItemToTimelineIn.title: ItemToTimelineIn

MomentOut.description:
One moment on the viewer's timeline (YONDER-177, D-172): an activity's start
or end. `at` is its local wall-clock time as stored ("YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM", or a
bare date); `label` is what it's called ("Check-in", "Drop-off", "Departure").
MomentOut.title: MomentOut

PhrasesIn.description: Local phrases & register for one city (topic `language_local`).
PhrasesIn.title: PhrasesIn

count.description: How many library places it holds.
count.title: Count

PlaceListPatch.description: Only the fields sent change. Lists are shown by `position`, then age.
PlaceListPatch.title: PlaceListPatch

list_ids.description: Every list the place should be in; [] takes it out of them all.
list_ids.title: List Ids

complete.description: Add a space after it; false for a chip that still wants its value, like `kind:`.
complete.title: Complete

count.description: How many of the caller's places it matches; none for a chip.
count.title: Count

insert.description: The text that replaces q[start:end], e.g. `list:"Date night"`.
insert.title: Insert

kind.description: chip, kind, list, city or country.
kind.title: Kind

label.description: What to show, e.g. "Restaurant" or "Lisbon, Portugal".
label.title: Label

PlanOut.description:
The budget beside what was actually spent (D-181). Only `actual` is the
trip's real cost; settle-up uses actual expenses alone (D-178).
PlanOut.title: PlanOut

seen_version.description: The last version whose notes the caller closed, on any device.
seen_version.title: Seen Version

admins.description: Setup notes for admins; always empty for anyone else.
admins.title: Admins

date.description: YYYY-MM-DD; none for a version not out yet.
date.title: Date

ReviewFieldOut.description: One editable field of a capture (same specs as the web detail pane).
ReviewFieldOut.title: ReviewFieldOut

ReviewItemDetail.description: GET /review/{id}: everything the review screen shows and edits.
ReviewItemDetail.title: ReviewItemDetail

SafetyTransportIn.description:
Safety & Transport for one city (topic `safety`, 4.5) — the same
structure the local resolver stores, so it renders as headed subsections.
SafetyTransportIn.title: SafetyTransportIn

SavedPlaceBatchIn.description:
Save a list of places in one call (a Google list, a Takeout export). Safe to
send twice: each place is saved at most once, and anything filed or removed
earlier is skipped and reported.
SavedPlaceBatchIn.title: SavedPlaceBatchIn

SavedPlaceFileIn.description:
File a saved place to a trip as a timeline activity. All optional: with no
date it lands undated (sorts last) to be scheduled later.
SavedPlaceFileIn.title: SavedPlaceFileIn

SavedPlaceIn.description:
Save a place. Either a Google/Apple Maps `url` for the server to parse, or
the details the app already resolved on the phone (MapKit, D-166); anything
supplied alongside a url overrides what the url yielded.
SavedPlaceIn.title: SavedPlaceIn

SavedPlacePatch.description:
Edit a saved place. Only the fields sent change; "" clears a to-do, a visit
or a locality. A locality sent here wins over any lookup (D-215).
SavedPlacePatch.title: SavedPlacePatch

SettlementIn.description: `from_id` paid `to_id` back. Currency defaults to the trip's.
SettlementIn.title: SettlementIn

TravelerPlanOut.description: One traveller's budget beside their share of what was spent (D-184).
TravelerPlanOut.title: TravelerPlanOut

TripRateOut.description:
One row of the trip's shared rate table (D-195): 1 `currency` = `rate`
`quote` for `rate_date`; `as_of` is the day the feed published it.
TripRateOut.title: TripRateOut

UserOut.description: The user payload (the API contract the app decodes — YONDER-58).
UserOut.title: UserOut

info.description: Every route needs a bearer token (or a web session); all data is scoped to the signed-in user.
info.title: Run·dere API

get.description: The timeline activity types and the `values` fields each one takes.

schema.title: Response Api Activity Types Api V1 Activity Types Get

put.description:
Set, change or clear your email — where password-reset links go. As on
the web (/account/email): a local account must give its current password
(a hijacked session must not be able to redirect resets). First-party only.
Removing it is allowed (D-220); `reset_note` then says what that means.

Turn support access on (for `duration`: 24h, 7d or standing) or off, as on
the web (D-211). Audited, and clears the first-sign-in question. First-party
only (the app or the web), never a connected app.

get.description:
The sign-in choices for THIS host, unauthenticated, for the app's login
screen (YONDER-180): the same per-host rules as the web login
(_login_options, YONDER-164). The host is the one the request was made to —
never a forwarded or proxy-supplied identity header. An older server
answers 404, which the app reads as "password only".

post.description:
Share-to-app: a Maps place or directions link, a webpage URL, or shared
page HTML. Owned by the caller (D-120). Links are routed as the capture
page routes them (D-209): a PLACE link becomes a saved place (D-166/167),
so a Google short link is expanded first, because the short form looks the
same for a place and for directions.

A new address; the old one stops working at once. First-party only: a
connected app can't retire the address your forwarding rules use.

Capture a file — a booking PDF, a calendar .ics or a saved .eml — for
iPad drag-and-drop, the Share Extension and the web (YONDER-179). It's
virus-scanned and stored (D-196), then extracted like any capture. Your
exact same file again returns the first one (`duplicate`), with no new
capture. 503 when file capture is off or the scanner is down; 413 too big
or over quota; 415 not a PDF/.ics/.eml; 422 unsafe.

parameters.description: Your local wall-clock time, YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM. Timeline times have no zone, so the app sends the device's time; the server's own clock is used when omitted.
parameters.name: now

schema.description: Your local wall-clock time, YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM. Timeline times have no zone, so the app sends the device's time; the server's own clock is used when omitted.
schema.title: Now

parameters.description: How far ahead `upcoming` looks, in hours.
parameters.name: window_h

schema.description: How far ahead `upcoming` looks, in hours.
schema.title: Window H

get.description:
Your captured files, newest first, with how much of your quota they use.
`enabled` says whether this server takes files at all.

delete.description: Delete your file now. What was extracted from it stays.

get.description:
The file itself — yours only, always as a download, never shown inline
(a PDF's scripts must never run in the app; D-196). 410 once removed.
A process/commit job's progress. Only its starter can see it.

The caller's own entries (own-only, D-134), newest day first. Optionally
scoped to one trip or an entry_date range.

schema.title: Response Api Journal List Api V1 Journal Get

post.description:
Create one journal entry owned by the caller. entry_date + captured_at are
the minimum stamps (defaulted here when omitted); geo is optional (D-142).
Writes are stateless about connectivity — offline queuing is the mobile
client's outbox (SPEC-6 D-135), not this endpoint.

patch.description:
Edit the caller's own entry. To change the trip link set attach_trip=true
(trip_id null detaches, a value re-attaches) — this makes an explicit intent
out of the nullable field so a normal patch never accidentally detaches.

post.description:
Fork an entry to apply the same note to another trip (D-133). The copy is
independent; `duplicated_from` records the origin.

get.description: Your discovery profile — what Discover (and your agents) research with.

The caller's library, newest first, each with a suggested trip, the trips
it is on and the lists it is in.

schema.title: Response Api Place List Api V1 Places Get

post.description:
Save a place for the caller. Safe to repeat or retry (an offline outbox, a
double tap): 201 when it was added, 200 when it was already there or had been
filed or removed, with `outcome` saying which. `activity_type` and `list_ids`
sort it as it's saved (D-236).

Save many places in one call. Each item is judged and committed on its own:
a bad item is reported, not fatal, and sending the same list again adds
nothing. Use `dry_run` first to see what would happen.

get.description:
The caller's lists in their order, each with how many places it holds. A
place's `list_ids` point here. Own-only (D-166, D-213): nobody else's lists
ever appear, admins' included.

schema.title: Response Api Place Lists Api V1 Places Lists Get

post.description: A new list, at the end of the caller's lists.

delete.description: Delete a list. Its places stay in the library (D-213).

patch.description: Rename a list, change its emoji or description, or move it (`position`).

get.description:
Suggestions for the Places search box as the person types (SPEC-11, D-235):
the place kinds after `kind:`, the caller's own lists after `list:`, the
cities and countries they've saved after `city:` and `country:`, and the
chips themselves before a colon. Replace `q[start:end]` with an item's
`insert`, then a space when it's `complete`. Own-only (D-166).

parameters.description: Where the caret is in q; the end when omitted.
parameters.name: cursor

schema.description: Where the caret is in q; the end when omitted.
schema.title: Cursor

patch.description:
Edit a saved place. A changed address places the pin when the place has
none (a street-level match only; nothing changes when there's no geocoder).

post.description: File a saved place to a trip (see `file_place`).

put.description:
Sort a place: make the lists it's in exactly `list_ids` (D-236). Safe to
repeat. Every list must be the caller's; one that isn't 404s and nothing
changes. A place in no list and on no trip is Unsorted.

get.description:
What changed in each version (SPEC-8 §14, D-234). By default only what the
caller hasn't seen yet, newest first and at most five, the same as the web's
What's new dialog: show it, then POST /release-notes/seen. `seen_version` is
shared with the web, so nobody is shown the same notes twice.

parameters.description: Every released version, newest first, instead of only the ones the caller hasn't seen.
parameters.name: all

schema.description: Every released version, newest first, instead of only the ones the caller hasn't seen.
schema.title: All

post.description: The caller has seen the notes up to the running version (D-234).

get.description:
Reusable agent instructions that research part of a trip and save it
to Discover over MCP (also served as MCP prompts).
The kit as a skill zip, to add to an agent that takes skills.

post.description:
Log the caller's approved captures to AirTrail + AdventureLog — only
their own (an admin: + ownerless ones), never anyone else's (D-211).
`dry_run: true` (default) returns the exact plan and writes nothing;
`dry_run: false` starts the irreversible write as a job (202 + JobOut).

Extract + resolve the caller's captures waiting in the pipeline (the web
"Process new captures"): their own — an admin's run also covers
ownerless captures and users who share. Returns a job to poll at GET /api/v1/jobs/{id}.

get.description:
One capture with its editable fields, who-flew / who-is-this-for
options, the trips it can be filed into, and what it would write.

patch.description:
Correct a capture: `fields` {path: value} (paths from GET's `fields`;
each change becomes a field lock), `passengers` (flights, identity ids),
`traveler_ids` (others, from GET's `who`). Re-resolves on change.
`approve: true` then approves it if it now resolves ("Save & approve").

post.description:
Stage a capture for logging (nothing is written yet — see /review/commit).
`ok: false` when it doesn't resolve yet; the item says why.

Link a capture to one of the user's trips (filing rule, see
assign_capture_to_trip).
Take a capture off the pipeline; it writes nothing.
Take back an approval that hasn't been logged yet.

schema.title: Response Api Trips Api V1 Trips Get

post.description: Plan a cost yourself (it's kept straight away).
Save budget research as drafts (see BudgetBatchIn).

Start the caller's Discovery run (in the background) and return its
status to poll. No body: the whole suite. `topic` (+ `place_key`): just
that — e.g. the weather, or the weather for one city — without redoing
the rest. Already running: that run's status, no second run. An ended
trip: 409 with the reason (D-157).

get.description:
The places the caller's Discovery would research on this trip (Refine
Discovery, YONDER-264): derived from the trip's own activities, with home and
the caller's own exclusions marked. Check this, exclude what you don't want,
then start a run.

put.description:
Exclude (`excluded: true`) or include again one place for the caller's
Discovery on this trip. Idempotent. Only a place the trip actually has (404
otherwise). Excluding drops that place's draft findings. Returns the list.

get.description: Poll the caller's run. When `running` turns false, reload the trip.

post.description: Put a Discover place/event/activity on the timeline, filled in from the item.

get.description:
The trip's costs you're on: expenses, balances and the suggested settle-up
payments, and the planned budget (D-183).

put.description:
Change the currency balances are shown in (D-176, D-195): costs convert
again from the trip's rate table at their own day. Rates you entered were
against the old currency, so they are cleared and need entering again.

post.description:
Comment on an expense you're on or entered (D-185). Anyone who can see the
expense can join the discussion, view-only shares included.

Save an AI agent's research into the caller's own Discover tab. The
agent is named after the bearer credential used (OAuth app / API token).
Add a custom line to the caller's own packing list.

patch.description: Check off / edit ONE of the caller's own packing lines (the phone use case).

post.description: Generate/regenerate the CALLER's own packing plan (per-user, D-123).

409.description: No packing profile yet: send the person to `url`.

post.description:
Fetch ONE currency's rate for a day (default today) onto the trip's shared
rate table (YONDER-237/242, D-195), then convert your costs in that currency
that had no rate yet. Costs that already have a rate keep it. On an ended
trip it's always today's rate (no backdating). 422 when no rate can be had.
Record that one traveller paid another back (D-177).

get.description:
The trip timeline as a shareable PDF itinerary — identical to the web
export (server-rendered). The flags choose what goes in (SPEC-8 §13,
D-233); left out, each keeps the PDF older app builds already get.
`packing` and `discover` add the caller's own list and Discover research,
never for a viewer; repeat `topic` to keep only those Discover topics.
